rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only deeds done to earn God's pleasure and reward in the hereafter carry weight on Judgment Day; deeds lacking these ends count as evil and have no weight.
rows.anchor: only those deeds will have weight on the Day of Judgement which are done to earn God’s pleasure and reward in the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction uses taḍmīn because its verb and preposition do not collocate; the implied sense includes denial of revelations and wronging oneself.
rows.anchor: There exists a taḍmīn (suppression of meaning) because the verb and the preposition do not collocate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed construction lets the verse express a comprehensive meaning in few words.
rows.anchor: The advantage of this taḍmīn is that a comprehensive meaning can be espoused in a few words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression for granting authority means giving political authority in a land, as it does in the account of Joseph.
rows.anchor: to grant political authority in the land.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ‘land’ is general, here it refers to the Haram, where Quraysh held political power.
rows.anchor: it refers to the area of Ḥaram in which they held political sway.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Sources of livelihood’ means sustenance and blessings available to the Arabs generally and Quraysh particularly.
rows.anchor: The expression “sources of livelihood” refer to the means of sustenance and blessings available to the Arabs in general and the Quraysh in particular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an discusses these blessings in several places, including the safe sanctuary drawing produce from everywhere; the author refers readers to his Baqarah exegesis for details.
rows.anchor: These blessings are mentioned in the Qur’ ān at a number of instances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about seldom being grateful states the consequence implied by the blessings just mentioned.
rows.anchor: The words “yet seldom are you grateful” depict what actually was meant to be stated after the things mentioned prior to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Ishmael's invocations and the House of God brought Quraysh political authority and generous provision.
rows.anchor: because of the invocations of Abraham (sws) and Ishmael (sws) and the House of God that the Quraysh were blessed with political authority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite these gifts, Quraysh were ungrateful and followed Satan, who succeeded in the trials he imposed on them.
rows.anchor: Instead of God, they followed Satan, as will be shown ahead. He was successful in whatever trials he wanted to inflict them with.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam–Satan episode explains the history of hostility between Satan and Adam's descendants and points to its cause.
rows.anchor: It shows the history of the enmity between Adam and his progeny with Satan and his accomplices.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account shows that Satan is granted life until the Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: It also shows that Satan will be kept alive until the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan vows revenge against Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: It also depicts the promise he has made to take revenge from the progeny of Adam (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's hostility arose from jealousy after God commanded him to honor Adam; his arrogant refusal led to humiliating expulsion and fueled his anger.
rows.anchor: The reason of Satan’s enmity with Adam (sws) and his progeny is because of his jealousy with them which arose when he was asked to honour them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After arrogantly rejecting the command, Satan was expelled and, in anger, sought respite until the Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: Ultimately, overcome with anger as a result of this expulsion, he requested God to be given respite until the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's animosity comes from humanity being preferred over him; he seeks respite to prove that preference wrong, and humans who support him effectively testify that God chose them wrongly.
rows.anchor: the real animosity which Satan has with mankind is because of the latter being given preference over him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By joining Satan's conflict with them, people make their own deeds testify that God wrongly preferred humanity over him.
rows.anchor: through their own deeds they bear witness that God had wrongly preferred them over Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is a continuing conflict between Adam's descendants and Satan, who is allowed to use lures and whisper evil until Judgement Day; the outcome is then decided.
rows.anchor: this world is a place of conflict between Adam’s progeny and Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's real aim is to turn people from monotheism; he lies in ambush, expects to mislead most people, and predicts their ingratitude to God.
rows.anchor: the real target of Satan in his onslaught is to make human beings deviate from the path of monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's failures proved Satan's prediction about mankind correct, making them liable for the evil fate God announced in reply to his challenge.
rows.anchor: Hence they have become worthy of the evil fate God had referred to while replying to the ultimatum of Satan:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaqa means to design; used alone it includes creation's consequences and connections, while accompanying terms narrow it to its literal meaning.
rows.anchor: The word ﺧﻠﻖmeans “to design” something.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘creating’ and ‘giving form’ denote creation's initial design and its final form and perfection.
rows.anchor: The initial phase of every creation is its design ad its final phase is the form and perfection given to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Quraysh, who are being reminded of human creation's phases and the trials ordained for them.
rows.anchor: Here the addressees, as indicated earlier, are the Quraysh. They are being informed of the about the phases of creation of human beings and of the trials ordained for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's story belongs to humanity as a whole because he is the father of humankind.
rows.anchor: Adam (sws) is the father of all humankind. Hence his anecdote is not solely his; it is that of the whole humankind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is the title of the jinn who deceived Adam and rebelled against God by disobeying Him.
rows.anchor: who had deceived Adam (sws). He was from among the jinn and had become rebellious by disobeying God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human and jinn followers of Iblis are treated as his progeny and are called Satans in the Qur'an; Satan is not an independent creation.
rows.anchor: It for such humans and jinn that the Qur’ān uses the word “Satan.” It is not an independent creation, as has been explained in Sūrah al-Baqarah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse, adding lā after mā manaʿaka is redundant because negation is implicit, but it heightens the rebuke; the parallel in Ṣād 38:75 lacks it.
rows.anchor: since the meaning of negation is already found in the expression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words ‘when I had ordered you’ show that Adam had no intrinsic entitlement to prostration; God conferred that status.
rows.anchor: Adam (sws) was not worthy of being prostrated before in the absolute sense. It was God Who made him so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration before Adam was in effect prostration before God, since it was performed at God's command.
rows.anchor: prostration before him was actually prostration before God because it was done at His behest.
